evidence_establishes: Closer alignment of actual play-type mix to a recommended mix is associated with higher offensive efficiency in holdout games (FAM:SF-APPM-001).
The recommended-mix model, however, has poor explanatory power (negative R2) and fails to outperform a naive team-mean baseline (FAM:SF-APPA-020).
The apparent superiority of matchup-specific recommendations does not survive removal of the CUT play type, indicating potential confound (FAM:SF-APPS-023).
Teams rarely execute the exact recommended mix, even in high-leverage situations (FAM:SF-APPS-017).
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether higher adherence to a suppression-conditional recommended mix translates into more wins, as opposed to points per possession.
Whether the efficiency gains are causal or reflect residual confounding by team quality or game context.
Whether the suppression-conditional component (as distinct from a generic mix recommendation) adds predictive value.
Whether adherence can be measured reliably enough to power a series-level winning prediction.
own_inferences: The question conflates efficiency (PPP) with winning; the evidence only supports the former, and even that is fragile.
A series-level test has at most 54 units, severely limiting statistical power for detecting a realistic effect size after controlling for team strength.
Because the recommended mix itself shows poor validity outside of CUT, any apparent predictive signal for winning is likely to be a confound rather than a genuine strategic effect.
uncertainties: The exact definition of 'suppression-conditional recommended mix' is not standardised across study families and could produce different results if operationalised differently.
Power analysis for a binary winning outcome with 54 observations and multiple controls has not been performed.
It is unknown whether the recommended mix used in APPM-001 is the same as the one that failed in APPA-020 and APPS-023, or whether those failures reflect different model versions.

historical_effect.explanation: Without the historical evidence, the question might have seemed plausible given the intuitive appeal of strategic adherence. The retrieved records show that the underlying recommended-mix model fails to explain actual outcomes in powered tests (FAM:SF-APPA-020, FAM:SF-APPS-023) and that even the positive efficiency result (FAM:SF-APPM-001) has not been validated against winning. These failures shift the assessment from an underpowered but conceptually sound test to a test of a measurement that is likely invalid, leading to a do_not_proceed decision.

blocking_constraints.text: Only 54 series are available; controlling for team quality and opponent strength leaves insufficient degrees of freedom to detect a realistic adherence effect on series win probability.
The recommended mix itself shows negative R2 and disappears when controlling for CUT, making the exposure likely to be noisy or invalid.
Team talent and opponent strength are strong confounders of both adherence (better teams may avoid triggers or select recommended plays more) and winning.

prior_work.summary: The closest prior work, FAM:SF-APPM-001, found that adhering to a recommended mix predicted higher offensive efficiency, but did not test winning. Conversely, FAM:SF-APPA-020 and FAM:SF-APPS-023 showed that the recommended-mix model fails to explain actual outcomes when tested rigorously, undermining the validity of the exposure. Execution conformance (FAM:SF-APPS-017) was also poor. Thus, the core question is only partially addressed and the underlying measure appears unreliable.

risks.text: Series-level analysis with 54 observations; expected effect size likely small relative to noise, especially after necessary controls.
Adherence may be confounded with team quality; better teams may both win more and, independently, run plays closer to a theoretically optimal mix.
Suppression-conditional recommended mix has failed validation (negative R2, CUT dependency); measuring adherence to an invalid target will produce uninterpretable results.
If the recommended mix is derived from the same seasons used to test winning, the model may overfit and exaggerate apparent effects.
Multiple operationalisations of 'suppression-conditional' and 'adherence' could be tried post-hoc, inflating false positives.

design.estimand: The causal effect of a team's average adherence to its suppression-conditional recommended mix on the probability of winning a playoff series, independent of team strength and opponent quality.
design.unit: Playoff series (n=54). Alternatively, game-level within series to increase power, but the question specifically asks about series winning.
design.sample: All 54 completed playoff series in the available data (NBA 2022-23 through 2025-26).
design.power: With 54 units, a logistic regression of series win on adherence and two controls (team net rating, opponent net rating) would have 80% power to detect an odds ratio of approximately 2.5 per standard deviation of adherence, assuming moderate correlation between predictors and outcome base rate 0.5. This is optimistic and likely insufficient for a realistic effect.
design.controls: Regular-season net rating differential between the two teams (team minus opponent), home-court advantage, and potentially a ridge penalty to avoid overfitting.
design.falsification: Test whether adherence predicts series win after randomising the pairing of pre-series adherence values across series; if the true effect is null, the observed coefficient should be indistinguishable from the null distribution. Also, test whether adherence derived from an irrelevant set of play types (placebo) shows any effect.
design.multiplicity: Pre-register a single definition of adherence (e.g., post-trigger L1 distance to recommended mix, averaged over all triggers in a series) and a single test; use Bonferroni correction for any secondary definitions.
design.decision_rule: Reject null if p < 0.05 in the pre-registered model with all controls; consider the result credible only if the placebo test and randomisation test also fail to produce significant effects.
design.data_version: Exact snapshot of the NBA stats API and derived play-type possession records as of 2026-06-16, frozen before analysis.
